text:
On the headland above Brevik, three white dishes still turn slowly against the grey of the North Sea, as they have for decades, tracking objects that most residents will never see. The station was built in an era of cautious public science, passed between caretakers, and has often seemed a place waiting for a purpose.

That purpose arrived on 14 March 2031, when Orbiton Systems formally signed a lease on the site. The 12-year agreement, valued at 48 million euros, covers all three antenna dishes and the control building. Marit Solvang, Director of Ground Operations at Orbiton Systems, confirmed the arrangement.

The terms appear in the Brevik Station Lease Agreement (Filing No. BGS-2031-07), published by the station's owning consortium. For a station long defined by uncertainty, twelve years offers something rare: a horizon.
